dublinCore.title: DFT Explorer: Probing a Signal with Rotating Phasors
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Discrete Fourier transform
Inverse DFT
Phasors
Orthogonality
Frequency domain
dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that builds each DFT value X[k] = sum x[n] e^(-j2 pi kn/N) visually: a unit circle shows the phasor for every sample, a complex plane adds the products x[n] e^(-j2 pi kn/N) head to tail so the running-sum arrow ends at X[k], and a bar chart mirrors |X[k]| with bin k highlighted. Animate and Step walk through n = 0..N-1, and an Inverse DFT mode rebuilds x[n] from bins the student clicks and shows the error and the energy kept.

searchKeywords: DFT as a sum of rotated samples

learningObjectives: Explain how X[k] is formed by multiplying each sample x[n] by a phasor that turns k/N of a revolution per sample and adding the products
Predict the non-zero DFT values of a sum of whole-bin sinusoids: AN/2 at bins m and N - m, or AN when m = 0 or m = N/2
Distinguish a matching bin, where the products line up and add, from a non-matching bin, where they close into a loop, and relate this to the orthogonality of the DFT phasors
Interpret the phase of X[k]: a cosine gives a real X[m] and a sine gives X[m] = -jAN/2
Analyze an inverse DFT built from a subset of bins by predicting its error and energy, and explain why bins k and N - k must be kept together for a real result
prerequisites: Complex numbers in polar form and Euler's formula

misconceptions.misconception: A cosine at bin m makes one spike at m
misconceptions.correction: A real cosine is the sum of two counter-rotating phasors, so it appears at bins m and N - m, each AN/2 tall (or one bin of height AN when m = 0 or N/2)
misconceptions.evidence: The default spectrum shows bars at 2, 5, 11 and 14; at k = N - m the unit circle turns counter-clockwise, and removing only one bin of a pair in Inverse DFT mode makes x_r[n] complex

misconceptions.misconception: If k does not match a frequency in the signal, X[k] is small but not zero
misconceptions.correction: For whole-bin sinusoids the DFT phasors are orthogonal and the sum is exactly zero; non-zero leakage needs a frequency between bins
misconceptions.evidence: With the default signal and k = 3 the green chain closes into a loop and the read-out is X[3] = 0.00 + j0.00

accessibility.screenReaderScript: DFT explorer. A stem plot shows an N-point signal x[n] built from up to three sinusoids. A unit circle shows the phasor e^(-j2 pi k n/N) for every n, a second plot shows its real and imaginary parts, and a complex plane adds the products x[n] times the phasor head to tail, so the running-sum arrow ends at X[k]. A bar chart shows |X[k]| for every bin with bin k highlighted. Controls: bin k slider, frequency and amplitude of each sinusoid, N, Animate and Step buttons, and an Inverse DFT checkbox that rebuilds x[n] from the bars you click.

controls.label: Bin k
controls.description: Chooses the DFT bin k, i.e. the probing phasor e^(-j2 pi kn/N); clicking a spectrum bar also sets it

controls.label: x1 frequency
controls.description: Waveform and bin of component 1: cos at m = 0..N/2 or sin at m = 1..N/2-1

controls.label: x2 frequency
controls.description: Waveform and bin of component 2 (same options as component 1)

controls.label: x3 frequency
controls.description: Waveform and bin of component 3 (same options as component 1)

controls.label: A1
controls.description: Amplitude of component 1 (0 turns it off)

controls.label: A2
controls.description: Amplitude of component 2 (0 turns it off)

controls.label: A3
controls.description: Amplitude of component 3 (0 turns it off)

controls.label: N
controls.description: DFT length; changing it clamps the component bins to the new range and restarts the inverse-DFT selection

controls.label: Animate / Pause / Resume
controls.description: Adds the products x[n] e^(-j2 pi kn/N) one sample at a time (0.7 s, 0.45 s or 0.26 s per sample for N = 8, 16, 32)

controls.label: Step
controls.description: Adds one product per click; after a finished sum it starts again at n = 0

controls.label: Inverse DFT
controls.description: Rebuilds x[n] from the bins that are kept (click bars to toggle), shows the error e[n] = x[n] - Re x_r[n], the energy kept, and warns when x_r[n] is complex

visualElements.description: Stem plot of x[n] (blue); in inverse mode the real part of the reconstruction x_r[n] is drawn as maroon rings
Real (purple) and imaginary (orange) parts of the phasor e^(-j2 pi kn/N), or the red error e[n] in inverse mode (screens at least 600 px wide)
Unit circle with one point per sample at e^(-j2 pi kn/N), labelled with n, and a gold radius for the sample being added
Complex plane with the products added head to tail (green) and the running-sum arrow (maroon) ending at X[k]
Bar chart of |X[k]| for k = 0..N-1 with bin k highlighted in gold and a dashed divider at N/2; bars are clickable

model.description: Builds x[n] from up to three whole-bin sinusoids, evaluates the DFT directly from its definition, draws the running sums S_k(n) = sum_{i<=n} x[i] e^(-j2 pi k i/N), and rebuilds x_r[n] from a selected set of bins with the inverse DFT
equations: x[n] = sum_i A_i cos(2 pi m_i n/N) or A_i sin(2 pi m_i n/N)
X[k] = sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] e^(-j 2 pi k n/N)
x_r[n] = (1/N) sum_{k kept} X[k] e^(+j 2 pi k n/N)
cos(2 pi m n/N) -> X[m] = X[N-m] = N/2 (X[m] = N when m = 0 or N/2)
sum_n e^(j 2 pi (k-m) n/N) = N if k = m (mod N), else 0
algorithms: Direct O(N^2) DFT and inverse DFT

instructionalStrategies: Predict X[k] before moving the bin slider
Step through the sum one sample at a time
Contrast a matching and a non-matching bin side by side
Remove bins to see the error and the energy kept
extensions: Allow non-integer frequencies to show spectral leakage
Add a window function and compare the chains
